title: SSC and Turbidity Relationship
text:
Sacramento River at Freeport
Start with the raw values:


Code
ls_ssc_turb$FPT %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ssc, y = turbidity_mean)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  labs(
    title = "Sacramento River at Freeport",
    subtitle = "SSC vs. Daily Average Turbidity, Original values"
  )









Try log-log transformation:


Code
ls_ssc_turb$FPT %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = log(ssc), y = log(turbidity_mean))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  labs(
    title = "Sacramento River at Freeport",
    subtitle = "SSC vs. Daily Average Turbidity, Log-transformed values"
  )










Initial Model
The relationship between SSC and Turbidity looks much clearer with the log-transformed data. Here is a simple linear model predicting Turbidity with SSC.


Code
df_ssc_turb_fpt <- ls_ssc_turb$FPT |>
  mutate(across(c(ssc, turbidity_mean), list(log = log)))

lm_ssc_turb_fpt <- lm(turbidity_mean_log ~ ssc_log, data = df_ssc_turb_fpt)
summary(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)



Call:
lm(formula = turbidity_mean_log ~ ssc_log, data = df_ssc_turb_fpt)

Residuals:
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-2.23342 -0.26795 -0.02424  0.26768  2.54690 

Coefficients:
             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept) -0.449052   0.023824  -18.85   <2e-16 ***
ssc_log      0.847774   0.007721  109.80   <2e-16 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 0.5106 on 4887 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.7116,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.7115 
F-statistic: 1.206e+04 on 1 and 4887 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16


Model diagnostics:


Code
check_model(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)











Code
check_heteroscedasticity(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)


Warning: Heteroscedasticity (non-constant error variance) detected (p < .001).


Code
shapiro.test(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt))



    Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)
W = 0.96596, p-value < 2.2e-16


Code
check_normality(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)


Warning: Non-normality of residuals detected (p < .001).




Code
acf(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt))









Code
Box.test(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt), lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box")



    Box-Ljung test

data:  residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)
X-squared = 26288, df = 20, p-value < 2.2e-16


Code
check_autocorrelation(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)


Warning: Autocorrelated residuals detected (p < .001).


The Shapiro-Wilk normality test shows that the residuals aren’t normal, and the Ljung-Box test indicates that the residuals are autocorrelated. Let’s try to improve the predictive power of the model by running a series of models adding 1 through 3 lag terms and compare how well they correct for autocorrelation.


Code
df_ssc_turb_fpt_lag <- df_ssc_turb_fpt |>
  mutate(
    ssc_log_lag1 = lag(ssc_log),
    ssc_log_lag2 = lag(ssc_log, 2),
    ssc_log_lag3 = lag(ssc_log, 3)
  )




Lag 1 Model


Code
lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag1 <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_lag |>
  drop_na(ssc_log_lag1) |>
  lm(turbidity_mean_log ~ ssc_log + ssc_log_lag1, data = _)

acf(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag1))









Code
Box.test(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag1), lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box")



    Box-Ljung test

data:  residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag1)
X-squared = 27513, df = 20, p-value < 2.2e-16




Lag 2 Model


Code
lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag2 <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_lag |>
  drop_na(ssc_log_lag1, ssc_log_lag2) |>
  lm(turbidity_mean_log ~ ssc_log + ssc_log_lag1 + ssc_log_lag2, data = _)

acf(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag2))









Code
Box.test(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag2), lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box")



    Box-Ljung test

data:  residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag2)
X-squared = 28262, df = 20, p-value < 2.2e-16




Lag 3 Model


Code
lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag3 <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_lag |>
  drop_na() |>
  lm(
    turbidity_mean_log ~ ssc_log + ssc_log_lag1 + ssc_log_lag2 + ssc_log_lag3,
    data = _
  )

acf(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag3))









Code
Box.test(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag3), lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box")



    Box-Ljung test

data:  residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_lag3)
X-squared = 304.86, df = 20, p-value < 2.2e-16




ARIMA Model
Adding up to 3 lag terms to the model appeared to do little to fix the serial autocorrelation. We’ll assess the possibility of using an ARIMA model, which requires a complete time series.


Code
df_ssc_turb_fpt |>
  as_tsibble(index = date) |>
  fill_gaps() |>
  filter(is.na(ssc_log))


# A tsibble: 161 x 10 [1D]
   station_abbr date         ssc turbidity_mean    wy month ys_storm storm_cat
   <chr>        <date>     <dbl>          <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>    <fct>    
 1 <NA>         2010-03-18    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 2 <NA>         2010-03-19    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 3 <NA>         2010-03-20    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 4 <NA>         2010-03-21    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 5 <NA>         2010-03-22    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 6 <NA>         2010-03-23    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 7 <NA>         2010-03-24    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 8 <NA>         2010-03-25    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
 9 <NA>         2010-03-26    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
10 <NA>         2010-03-27    NA             NA    NA    NA <NA>     <NA>     
# ℹ 151 more rows
# ℹ 2 more variables: ssc_log <dbl>, turbidity_mean_log <dbl>


There are 161 days with missing data in the time series. For now, we will use the simple linear model with log-transformed data to predict Turbidity from SSC despite the issues with non-normality and serial autocorrelation of the residuals. This is okay since we are only using the model for predictions, not to produce prediction intervals or for hypothesis testing.


Observed vs. Predicted
Plot the observed Turbidity values vs. the back-transformed model predictions (fitted values) to see how they compare and to check model performance.


Code
df_ssc_turb_fpt_mod <- df_ssc_turb_fpt |>
  mutate(
    fitted_vals = fitted(lm_ssc_turb_fpt),
    fitted_vals_bt = exp(fitted_vals)
  )

plt_obs_pred_fpt <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_mod |>
  ggplot(aes(x = turbidity_mean, y = fitted_vals_bt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs. Predicted",
    subtitle = "All data",
    x = "Observed",
    y = "Predicted"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

plt_obs_pred_fpt









Many of the predicted values from the model are lower than their associated observed values. This is most likely because we used a log-transformed response variable. In this case, back-transforming the model predictions provides the geometric mean or median when tends to underestimate the mean. We can try using the Smearing Estimator bias correction method to adjust the model predictions.


Code
df_ssc_turb_fpt_mod2 <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_mod |>
  mutate(
    fitted_vals_bt_adj = fitted_vals_bt * mean(exp(residuals(lm_ssc_turb_fpt)))
  )

plt_obs_pred_fpt_adj <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_mod2 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = turbidity_mean, y = fitted_vals_bt_adj)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs. Predicted and Adjusted",
    subtitle = "All data",
    x = "Observed",
    y = "Predicted & Adjusted"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  ylim(c(0, 175))

(plt_obs_pred_fpt + ylim(c(0, 175))) + plt_obs_pred_fpt_adj









This provides a slight improvement in the model predictions, but not much.


Just Winter-Early Spring
What if we restrict the data to the months when storms are most prevalent in our model since this is the time period we are most interested in for our analyses.


Code
df_sac_storm |>
  filter(ys_storm == "STORM") |>
  count(month)


# A tibble: 10 × 2
   month     n
   <dbl> <int>
 1     1   380
 2     2   353
 3     3   311
 4     4   119
 5     5    50

 7     7     1
 8    10     7

10    12   296


It looks like storms are most common during December - April, so we’ll use that time period.


Code
df_ssc_turb_fpt_wint <- df_ssc_turb_fpt |> filter(month %in% c(1:4, 12))




Code
df_ssc_turb_fpt_wint %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = log(ssc), y = log(turbidity_mean))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +

  labs(
    title = "Sacramento River at Freeport",
    subtitle = "SSC vs. Daily Average Turbidity, Log-transformed values, December - April"
  )

df_ssc_turb_fpt_wint_mod <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_wint |>
  mutate(
    fitted_vals = fitted(lm_ssc_turb_fpt_wint),
    fitted_vals_bt = exp(fitted_vals)

plt_obs_pred_fpt_wint <- df_ssc_turb_fpt_wint_mod |>

This seems to be slightly better than the model using all data, but not by much.


Specific Question from Brian S
In response to a specific question from Brian S, predict the change in suspended sediment needed to go from a Turbidity of 180 FNU to 20 FNU


Code
# Reverse regression relationship
lm_turb_ssc_fpt <- lm(ssc_log ~ turbidity_mean_log, data = df_ssc_turb_fpt)
summary(lm_turb_ssc_fpt)

lm(formula = ssc_log ~ turbidity_mean_log, data = df_ssc_turb_fpt)

Code
df_new_data <- tibble(turbidity_mean_log = log(c(20, 180)))
ls_new_data_conf <- predict(
  lm_turb_ssc_fpt,
  df_new_data,
  se.fit = TRUE,
  interval = "confidence"
)

ls_new_data_pred <- predict(
  lm_turb_ssc_fpt,
  df_new_data,
  se.fit = TRUE,
  interval = "prediction"
)

df_new_data_c <-
  bind_cols(
    df_new_data,
    as_tibble(ls_new_data_conf$fit),
    as_tibble_col(ls_new_data_pred$se.fit, column_name = "se")
  ) %>%
  rename(
    ssc_fit = fit,
    conf95_lower = lwr,
    conf95_upper = upr
  ) %>%
  bind_cols(as_tibble(ls_new_data_pred$fit)) %>%
  select(-fit) %>%
  rename(pred95_lower = lwr, pred95_upper = upr) %>%
  relocate(se, .after = last_col()) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), exp))

Code
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)

title: First Flush - Water Quality Analysis Plan
text:
Map


Code
# Import continuous WQ station coordinates
sf_stations <- read_sf(
  here("data/processed/spatial/first_flush_spatial_data.gpkg"),
  layer = "cont_wq_stations"
)

# Import continuous WQ station metadata
df_metadata <- readRDS(here("data/processed/wq/cont_wq_metadata.rds"))

# Add station names to station coordinates
sf_stations_c1 <- sf_stations %>%
  left_join(df_metadata, by = join_by(Source, Station_ID)) %>%
  relocate(Station_Name, .after = Station_ID) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), date))

# Define stations in consideration
df_stations_analysis <- tribble(
  ~Source         , ~Station_ID     ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11447650" ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "SRH"           ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11447905" ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11447890" ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "PPT"           ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11313460" ,
  "DWR-NCRO (WQ)" , "B9520000"      ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11313434" ,
  "DWR-NCRO (WQ)" , "B9545800"      ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11312685" ,
  "DWR-NCRO (WQ)" , "B9525100"      ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11313405" ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11312676" ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11313315" ,
  "DWR-NCRO (WQ)" , "B9529500"      ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11313240" ,
  "DWR-NCRO (WQ)" , "B9537800"      ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "MSD"           ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11304810" ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "RVB"           ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11455420" ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11337190" ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "MAL"           ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "HON"           ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "RYC"           ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "GZL"           ,
  "DWR-CEMP"      , "SJR"           ,
  "USGS"          , "USGS-11303500"
)

# Filter to stations in consideration
sf_stations_c2 <- sf_stations_c1 |>
  right_join(df_stations_analysis, by = join_by(Source, Station_ID))

# Add info for CLC station
sf_clc <-
  tibble(
    Parameter = c(
      "Water Temperature",
      "Specific Conductance",
      "Turbidity (NTU)",
      "Chlorophyll Fluorescence"
    ),
    Start = ymd(c("1988-03-04", "1987-01-01", "1988-03-10", "1988-03-07"))
  ) |>
  expand_grid(
    Source = "DWR-O&M",
    Station_ID = "CLC",
    Station_Name = "Clifton Court Forebay",
    Latitude = 37.829800,
    Longitude = -121.557400,
    Interval = "Daily",
    End = ymd(today())
  ) |>
  st_as_sf(
    coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),
    crs = 4326,
    sf_column_name = "geom"
  )

sf_stations_c3 <-
  bind_rows(sf_stations_c2, sf_clc) |>
  mutate(Region = replace_na(Region, "Out of Bounds"))

# Import Region polygons
sf_regions <-
  read_sf(
    here("data/processed/spatial/first_flush_spatial_data.gpkg"),
    layer = "design_regions"
  ) |>
  filter(Region != "Out of Bounds")

# Create color palettes for station points (using Source) and region polygons
pal_stations <- plasma(n = length(unique(sf_stations_c3$Source)))
pal_regions <- color("muted")(length(unique(sf_regions$Region)))

sf_stations_c3 |>
  distinct(Source, Station_ID, Station_Name, Region, geom) |>
  mapview(
    zcol = "Source",

title: Continuous Water Quality Station Maps
text:
Code
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(viridisLite)
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(htmltools)
library(DT)
library(here)
library(conflicted)

# Declare package conflict preferences
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter())

# Prevent mapview from dynamically switching to dark maps based on point color contrast
mapviewOptions(basemaps.color.shuffle = FALSE)



Import and Prepare Data


Code
# Import continuous WQ station coordinates
sf_stations <- read_sf(
  here("data/processed/spatial/first_flush_spatial_data.gpkg"),
  layer = "cont_wq_stations"
)

# Import continuous WQ station metadata
df_metadata <- readRDS(here("data/processed/wq/cont_wq_metadata.rds"))

# Add metadata to station coordinates
sf_stations_c1 <- sf_stations %>%
  left_join(df_metadata, by = join_by(Survey, Data_Source, Station_ID)) %>%
  relocate(Station_Name, .after = Station_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    across(where(is.Date), \(x) format(x, "%Y-%m-%d")),
    Survey = factor(Survey)
  )

# Import Strata polygons
sf_strata <-
  read_sf(
    here("data/processed/spatial/first_flush_spatial_data.gpkg"),
    layer = "design_strata"
  ) |>
  filter(!Stratum %in% c("Out of Bounds", "Central SF Bay", "South SF Bay"))

# Create color palettes for station points (using Survey) and region polygons
survey_names <- levels(sf_stations_c1$Survey)
pal_stations <-
  plasma(n = length(survey_names)) |>
  setNames(survey_names)




Interactive Maps


Code
ndf_maps <- sf_stations_c1 %>%
  nest(sf_data = everything(), .by = Parameter) %>%
  mutate(sf_data = map(sf_data, \(x) mutate(x, Survey = fct_drop(Survey)))) |>
  arrange(Parameter) %>%
  mutate(
    maps = map(
      sf_data,
      \(sf_obj) {
        local_levels <- levels(sf_obj$Survey)
        local_colors <- pal_stations[local_levels]

        mapview(
          sf_obj,
          zcol = "Survey",
          col.regions = unname(local_colors),
          label = "Station_Name",
          layer.name = "Survey",
          cex = 5
        ) +
          mapview(
            sf_strata,
            label = "Stratum",
            layer.name = "Strata",
            alpha.regions = 0.4,
            legend = FALSE
          )
      }
    )
  )
